inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 revenue of the two operating companies plus Corporate/Other on the guidance perimeter (EUR 22,554m, the base management uses for the 4-7% FY2026 organic growth guide). IFRS continuing revenue is EUR 22,873m; the EUR 319m difference is the residual Vamed Austrian activities, sold/exited at 31-Dec-2025, which are not part of the forward business. Pre-FMC-deconsolidation revenue (FY2022 EUR 40.8bn) is NOT used anywhere in the forward build.
inputs.share_count_basis: 563,237,277 ordinary shares; basic = diluted (FY2025 AR income statement, EPS 'basic and diluted'; no stock options outstanding, LTIP 2023 is cash-settled virtual shares). No buybacks since at least 2016. Held FLAT.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Net debt EXCLUDING lease liabilities, EUR 8,937m at 31-Dec-2025 (FY2025 AR net debt note: debt 1,601 + bonds 8,921 (incl. the EUR 592m FMC exchangeable bond at fair value) - cash 1,585 = 8,937; lease liabilities 1,411 excluded because leases are charged in the flows, treatment B). Including leases: 10,348 (2.7x EBITDA as reported).
inputs.fcf_basis: Reported FCF = OCF continuing 2,606 - capex 1,105 (FY2025 cash flow statement), the CSV series. Levered and before lease principal. Unlevered owner FCF on the engine's basis: 2,606 + interest paid 368 - interest received 68 - net capex 986 (capex 1,105 less hospital capex subsidies 119) - lease principal 173 - lease interest 46 = ~EUR 1,700m (7.5% of revenue), flattered by a +EUR 267m working-capital release (payables/provisions +756). FMC dividends (121m) are in investing and are NOT in the flows; the FMC stake is in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR share-based compensation note: EUR 89m expense (2024: 51m) for CASH-SETTLED plans (LTIP 2023 virtual shares, Management Board plans). It is already an operating expense inside EBITDA and is paid in cash, so it is neither added back nor dilutive; sbc_pct_path is held at 0 to avoid charging it twice. No equity-settled plans; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net debt company: interest income (FY2025 116m P&L, 68m received) is not deducted; the engine flows are unlevered (pre-interest), debt is subtracted in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: No share repurchases (ShareRepurchases 0 every year FY2016-FY2025). The flat count is a fact, not a modelling convention: there is no equity-settled dilution to fund.
inputs.fx_note: Statements EUR, Xetra quote EUR. Kabi has material USD (North America) and LatAm exposure, translated in the filings; flows modelled at constant translation.
inputs.anchor_vintage_note: The latest Fresenius filing extracted is the FY2025 Annual Report (31-Dec-2025); the Q1/H1/Q3 2026 interim reports are not in Extracted/, so net debt and the share count are ten months old. The FMC share count in the bridge is fresher (FMC H1 2026 interim, 30-Jun-2026). Replace the balance-sheet anchors when the 2026 interims are extracted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 6.5% nominal EUR: risk-free 2.9% (10y Bund), ERP 5.0%, levered beta 1.0 (European healthcare asset beta ~0.7 at ~28% net-debt-to-EV, plus KGaA/foundation-controlled governance) -> cost of equity 7.9%; pre-tax cost of debt 4.0% (FY2025 interest expense 445m on ~10.5bn gross financial debt; 2.89% average coupon on the book, refinancing at higher rates) x (1-27%) = 2.9%; market weights 72/28 (market cap ~EUR 26bn, net debt incl. leases 10.3bn). Same WACC in all scenarios; risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash (principal 173 + interest 46 = 219m, 0.97% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (1,411m) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A before special items 1,098 less ROU depreciation 187 = 911, 4.0% of revenue) so the cash-tax EBIT is not charged the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI charged ONCE in the equity bridge (FY2025 continuing NCI share of net income 70m, book NCI 663m, mainly the minority in mAbxience and smaller Kabi/Helios subsidiaries) at ~14x NCI earnings = EUR 1,000m.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations (EUR WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in the bridge, matching-asset rule for the FMC stake, SBC-zero equity market). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US': Fresenius Kabi (IV generics/fluids, clinical nutrition, biosimilars, MedTech) and Helios (German and Spanish hospitals) are operating businesses with real FCF; it is not a bank, REIT or holdco, though the ~28.5% FMC equity-method stake is valued separately at market (sum of parts: operating DCF + listed stake). No MEMORY.md entry and no prior DCF: first valuation. STRUCTURAL BREAK: FY2023 deconsolidation of FMC (and the FY2024-25 Vamed exit) means pre-FY2023 revenue, FCF and growth rates are a different company; the forward build is anchored only on FY2025 continuing operations and FY2026 guidance. Margin anchors: FY2025 group EBIT before special items 2,595m (11.5%) + D&A 1,098m = EBITDA ~16.4% on 22,554m; FY2026 guide Kabi EBIT 16.5-17% and Helios 10-10.5% implies group EBIT ~12.0% -> pre-special EBITDA ~16.9%. The engine EBITDA margin is pre-IFRS-16-lease-relief equivalent: pre-special EBITDA less a recurring 0.6pp special-items cash leakage (restructuring, German hospital-reform and #FutureFresenius programme costs recur in practice). Year-1 base owner FCF ~EUR 1.74bn (7.4%), vs FY2025 unlevered ~1.70bn with a WC tailwind and vs the 'cash conversion slightly below 1' guide (~1.65bn levered + ~0.25bn after-tax interest). Base revenue is FY2025 and the balance sheet 31-Dec-2025; year 1 (FY2026) is ten months elapsed. Recent development per the Analysis JSON (not in extracted filings): Fresenius sold ~7.8m further FMC shares for ~EUR 300m in Aug-2026; that is a cash-for-shares swap at roughly market and is value-neutral in this bridge.

equity_bridge.note: Estimate: FY2025 AR says the international project-business exit carries high-three-digit-million total special items (largely incurred: -272m discontinued loss in 2025) and bank guarantees for performance commitments in the low-three-digit million range.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: post-deconsolidation organic revenue growth (FY2025 actual 7%, FY2026 guide 4-7%); midpoint-ish 5%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All 3y/5y CAGRs straddle the FY2023 FMC deconsolidation (revenue 40.8bn -> 22.3bn) and the Vamed exit, so they measure portfolio shrinkage, not growth. Equity 5y CAGR (2.4%) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs (all negative). None is usable as a forward rate; the selected rate is the continuing-operations organic growth.
historical_growth.notes: Annual rows FY2020-FY2025, EUR millions, CSV basis (FY2022 includes FMC; FY2023-25 continuing only). FCF = OCF - capex as reported; SBC adjustment is zero (cash-settled, already inside OCF) and interest income is not stripped (net debt), so the owner-FCF series equals the reported series. Continuing-only FY2024 restated -> FY2025 revenue +4.2% reported (+7% organic; FX and Vamed perimeter drag). Core EPS ex-FMC +12% cc in FY2025.

base.growth_note: FY2026 4.5% reported = ~5.5% organic (guide 4-7%) less ~1pp FX (USD weakness); Kabi mid-to-high single digit, Helios mid-single digit; fading to 2.5% by year 10.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-special EBITDA margin ~16.9% (2026 guide) less 0.6pp recurring special-items cash leakage = 16.3%, rising ~1pp by 2030 as Kabi moves into its raised 17-19% EBIT band (Biopharma at ~20%) and Helios reaches the bottom of its 10-12% band.
base.capex_note: Net of hospital capex subsidies (FY2025 gross 4.8%, net 4.3%); slightly higher for 'Rejuvenate' MedTech/biopharma capacity, easing later.
base.tax_note: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT: Germany ~30%, Spain 25%, US ~25%; FY2025 effective rate 26.6%.
base.wc_note: Negative capture: receivables + inventories (6.2bn) far exceed trade payables (1.3bn); FY2025's +267m WC release is not repeated.
base.terminal_cap_note: 16x: defensive, mid-single-digit-growth healthcare with regulated hospital pricing; Gordon at 6.5%/2% would be ~22.7x.

scenario_narratives.base: Fresenius delivers the 'Rejuvenate' plan roughly as guided: FY2026 organic growth ~5.5% (guide 4-7%), Kabi growing mid-to-high single digits with biosimilars (denosumab, tocilizumab, ustekinumab) and MedTech (Ivenix pumps, plasma-collection yields) lifting its EBIT margin into the raised 17-19% band, while Helios grows mid-single digits and recovers from the energy-relief roll-off to ~10.5-11% as German hospital reform consolidates sites into regional clusters. Group pre-special EBIT margin rises from 11.5% to ~13% by 2030, restructuring costs keep recurring at ~0.6% of revenue, capex stays ~4.5% net of subsidies, and growth fades to 2.5%. The FMC stake is worth its market price; no credit for further deleveraging beyond what the flows deliver.
scenario_narratives.bull: Biopharma doubles revenue by 2030 at ~20% EBIT margin as planned, MedTech scales in the US, and IV/nutrition benefit from US/EU supply-chain reshoring; Helios captures share as smaller German hospitals close under the reform and Quironsalud keeps compounding private-pay volumes in Spain. Revenue grows 6-6.5% for three years and the EBITDA margin reaches ~18.4% (group EBIT ~14%). Terminal growth 2.5% and an 18x cap, roughly where the market prices the business today.
scenario_narratives.bear: Generic-injectable price erosion (Sandoz, Hikma, Pfizer/Hospira, GPO consolidation), recurring US tariff and USD headwinds, and Chinese procurement changes stall Kabi's margin gains; biosimilar launches slip. Helios is squeezed by German reimbursement that lags wage inflation and by reform restructuring, staying below its 10% band. Revenue grows ~3% and the EBITDA margin erodes ~0.8pp, capex runs higher for reform-driven hospital consolidation, and the terminal is valued at 12x with 1.5% growth. Leverage stays inside the 2.5-3.0x corridor, so there is no solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because both segments are exposed to politically set reimbursement (German hospital reform, US GPO/tariff policy) and Kabi's core IV generics face structural price pressure. Base 50%: management met or beat raised targets in FY2024 and FY2025 and guides conservatively. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30% because it needs the biopharma pipeline and Helios reform to both deliver.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value post-#FutureFresenius Fresenius (Kabi + Helios) on unlevered owner FCF built from guided segment margins, with leases charged in the flows, cash-settled LTIP already inside EBITDA, minorities deducted once, and the ~28.5% FMC stake added at market rather than through its dividends. Pre-2023 history is a different (FMC-consolidated) company and is ignored for forward growth.
key_risks_to_valuation: Balance-sheet anchors are 31-Dec-2025 (2026 interims not extracted); ten months of FCF and any FMC share sales since are not in net debt
FMC stake value moves with FME.DE: +/- EUR 5 on FME is ~+/- EUR 0.68/share
Recurring special-items leakage (0.6pp) is a judgment; Fresenius has reported special items every year of the transformation
Terminal cap (16x) binds well below Gordon (~22.7x at 6.5%/2%): value is sensitive to the multiple a regulated hospital/generics group commands
NCI valued at ~14x earnings (EUR 1.0bn) rather than at a disclosed fair value
German hospital reform and Kabi US pricing are policy-driven, not forecastable from the filings
